newsitem.title: UK: Salt can undo good in blood pressure drugs -study.
newsitem.headline: Salt can undo good in blood pressure drugs -study.

text.p: Blacks who are overweight and who eat a lot of salt may be undoing the good done by medication for high blood pressure, researchers said on Tuesday.

Dr Elijah Saunders and colleagues at the University of Maryland School of Medicine said eating habits could explain why blood pressure medicines such as angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEI) sometimes does not work.

"When black patients consumed a reasonable amount of salt and were not overweight, the ACEI treatment satisfactorily controlled their blood pressure," Saunders told the 12th International Interdisciplinary Conference on Hypertension in Blacks.
"However, when overweight black patients consuming a high-salt diet were treated with ACEI monotherapy, we saw a 50 percent reduction in response rate."
About one in four people with high blood pressure are sensitive to salt, but this vulnerability is hard to detect.
Experts speaking at the conference called on restaurants and food processors to lower the amount of salt in their food to benefit the population in general.

"Lower salt intake by the population as a whole will help physicians control blood pressure among hypertensives identified with blood pressure sensitive to salt intake," said Albert Carr, president of the Circulatory Disease Centre in Augusta, Georgia.
Most people eat far more salt than they need anyway, researchers say.
